doc.title: Artie Shaw — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Early years: Cleveland, Aaronson, New York
title: Friendship with Bunny Berigan; playing lead alto on I Can't Get Started
summary: He played alto on Bunny's record, remembers jamming with him in Cleveland, and notes Bunny's drinking as an addiction.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: We’d do these. I did a few records. As a matter of fact, on Bunny—very . . . nobody knows this—on Bunny Berigan’s I Can’t Get Started, I played lead alto [saxophone] on that.
That’s right. The first recording of that.
Most people don’t know that. Bunny and I were great friends. If I had a date, I would ask Bunny to play.
Yeah, you made some nice records with Bunny.

We both knew each other very well. When I was in Cleveland, he’d come through when he was with Hal Kemp, and I would take him down to Central Avenue. We’d jam all night. He was drinking then, though. He was already starting. I wondered about that. In my book I talk about it too, in the book I’m doing.
I guess it was an ever-present problem for a lot of guys.
It’s an addiction, like any other addiction.
